

\# GitHub Copilot Instructions for D365FO (Metadata XML)



> \*\*Purpose\*\*: Steer GitHub Copilot to generate \*\*D365FO AOT metadata XML\*\* files (not X++ snippets) for core code objects. Use this as `copilot-instructions.md` or place it at `.github/copilot-instructions.md` in your repo.



This guide provides:

\- Authoring guidance for \*\*AOT XML\*\* (Tables, EDTs, Enums, Classes)

\- \*\*Complete XML examples\*\* you can adapt

\- Ready-to-paste \*\*prompt templates\*\*



> \*\*Note\*\*: These are simplified, human-readable XML templates compatible with typical D365FO/AOS metadata conventions. Real projects may have additional elements/attributes generated by the designer.



---



\## ✅ General Guidance for Copilot (XML)



\- Use a \*\*single root\*\* element named after the artifact type (e.g., `AxTable`, `AxEdt`, `AxEnum`, `AxClass`).

\- Always include \*\*Name\*\*, \*\*Label\*\*, and optional \*\*HelpText\*\*.

\- Use \*\*EDT\*\* names when defining field types (for tables) and set \*\*indexes\*\* and \*\*relations\*\* explicitly.

\- For classes, include \*\*Name/Label\*\* in metadata; method bodies are typically stored as X++ source, but you can embed simplified `<Source>` blocks when needed to keep everything in one file.

\- Do \*\*not\*\* declare system fields (`RecId`, `DataAreaId`, `RecVersion`)—they are system-managed.



---

\## 🔤 Example: EDT XML (`AxEdt`)



```xml

<AxEdt>

&nbsp; <Name>DemoId</Name>

&nbsp; <Label>@Demo:DemoId</Label>

&nbsp; <HelpText>@Demo:DemoIdHelp</HelpText>

&nbsp; <Type>String</Type>

```

\## 🧠 Example: Class XML (`AxClass`)



> In D365FO, the class \*\*metadata\*\* is stored in XML (name, labels, properties), while the \*\*X++ source\*\* is stored as code. If you want everything in a single file for scaffolding, include a `<Source>` element for illustrative purposes.



```xml

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>

<AxClass xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">

&nbsp;	<Name>AVADemoClass</Name>

&nbsp;	<SourceCode>

&nbsp;		<Declaration><!\[CDATA\[

internal final class AVADemoClass

{

}

]]></Declaration>

&nbsp;		<Methods>

&nbsp;			<Method>

&nbsp;				<Name>main</Name>

&nbsp;				<Source><!\[CDATA\[

&nbsp;   public static void main(Args \_args)

&nbsp;   {

&nbsp;       AVADemoClass demo = new AVADemoClass();

&nbsp;   }



]]></Source>

&nbsp;			</Method>

&nbsp;			<Method>

&nbsp;				<Name>run</Name>

&nbsp;				<Source><!\[CDATA\[

&nbsp;   public void run()

&nbsp;   {

&nbsp;       info("Hello, this is a demo class for Azure Virtual Agents integration!");

&nbsp;   }



]]></Source>

&nbsp;			</Method>

&nbsp;		</Methods>

&nbsp;	</SourceCode>

</AxClass>

```

\## 🧩 Optional: Form/Data Entity XML Pointers



\- \*\*Forms\*\* often reference `AxForm` with DataSources and Design controls—these are verbose. Start simple: Name/Label, one DataSource, and a Grid control bound to your `AxTable` fields.

\- \*\*Data entities\*\* (`AxDataEntity`) define data sources and staging; include Name, Label, and a list of fields mapping to your table.



---



\## 🧭 Prompt Templates for Copilot



Use these to ask Copilot for XML directly:



\- \*\*Table\*\*

&nbsp; > "Generate a D365FO \*\*AxTable XML\*\* named `DemoEntity` with fields `DemoId` (EDT), `Name`, `ItemId`, `Qty`, `Status` (enum `DemoStatus`), a primary/cluster index on `DemoId`, an alternate key on `Name`, a relation to `InventTable` on `ItemId`, and field groups `AutoLookup`/`AutoReport`."



\- \*\*EDT\*\*

&nbsp; > "Create an \*\*AxEdt XML\*\* for `DemoId` (string size 20, left aligned) with label/help."



\- \*\*Enum\*\*

&nbsp; > "Create an \*\*AxEnum XML\*\* named `DemoStatus` with elements `None=0`, `Active=1`, `Closed=2` and labels."



\- \*\*Class\*\*

&nbsp; > "Produce an \*\*AxClass XML\*\* for `DemoEntityService` (RunOn=Server, IsFinal=Yes) and embed a `<Source>` block with a static method `findByDemoId(DemoId)` that selects by `DemoId`."



---



\## 🔍 Quality Checklist (XML)



\- Root element corresponds to artifact type (`AxTable`, `AxEdt`, `AxEnum`, `AxClass`).

\- Includes \*\*Name\*\* and \*\*Label\*\*; optional \*\*HelpText\*\* is descriptive.

\- For tables: fields use \*\*EDT\*\* names; indexes declare uniqueness; relations reference existing tables.

\- XML is \*\*well-formed\*\* (matching tags, valid nesting, CDATA for any embedded code).

\- Avoid system-managed fields in table XML.



---



\## ℹ️ Notes



\- These examples are intentionally concise to be readable in code reviews and PRs.

\- When importing to Visual Studio, the designer may expand with additional metadata.

\- Align \*\*label IDs\*\* (e.g., `@Demo:...`) with your solution's label file prefix.

D365 Finance & Operations - AOT Query XML Metadata Schema Guide
Overview
This guide explains how to create XML metadata files for queries in D365FO AOT (Application Object Tree). The query XML file defines the structure, data sources, ranges, and sorting for database queries.
File Location

Path: YourModel/YourModel/AxQuery/[QueryName].xml
Example: MyModel/MyModel/AxQuery/DocuHistoryCleanupQuery.xml

XML Schema Structure
1. Root Element
xml<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<AxQuery xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" 
         xmlns="" 
         i:type="AxQuerySimple">
Attributes:

xmlns:i - XML Schema instance namespace (always the same)
xmlns - Default namespace (empty string)
i:type - Query type, typically AxQuerySimple

2. Query Name
xml<Name>YourQueryName</Name>
Rules:

Must match the XML filename (without .xml extension)
Use PascalCase naming convention
Include your module prefix for uniqueness

3. Source Code Section (Optional but Recommended)
xml<SourceCode>
    <Methods>
        <Method>
            <Name>classDeclaration</Name>
            <Source><![CDATA[
[Query]
public class YourQueryName extends QueryRun
{
}
]]></Source>
        </Method>
    </Methods>
</SourceCode>
Purpose:

Defines the query class that extends QueryRun
Uses [Query] attribute to mark it as a query
Wrapped in CDATA section to preserve code formatting
Can include additional methods like init(), executeQuery(), etc.

4. Data Sources Section
4.1 Root Data Source
xml<DataSources>
    <AxQuerySimpleRootDataSource>
        <Name>TableName</Name>
        <DynamicFields>Yes</DynamicFields>
        <Table>TableName</Table>
        
        <!-- Child elements -->
        <DataSources />
        <DerivedDataSources />
        <Fields />
        <Ranges>
            <!-- Range definitions -->
        </Ranges>
        <GroupBy />
        <Having />
        <OrderBy>
            <!-- OrderBy definitions -->
        </OrderBy>
    </AxQuerySimpleRootDataSource>
</DataSources>
Elements:

<Name> - Logical name for the data source (usually the table name)
<DynamicFields> - Values: Yes or No. Set to Yes to include all table fields
<Table> - Physical table name from AOT
<DataSources /> - For nested/joined data sources
<DerivedDataSources /> - For computed data sources
<Fields /> - Specific field selections (if not using DynamicFields)

4.2 Nested Data Sources (Joins)
xml<DataSources>
    <AxQuerySimpleEmbeddedDataSource>
        <Name>RelatedTable</Name>
        <DynamicFields>Yes</DynamicFields>
        <Table>RelatedTableName</Table>
        <JoinMode>InnerJoin</JoinMode>
        <Relations>
            <AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRelation>
                <Field>ForeignKeyField</Field>
                <JoinDataSource>ParentDataSource</JoinDataSource>
                <RelatedField>PrimaryKeyField</RelatedField>
            </AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRelation>
        </Relations>
        <DataSources />
        <Fields />
        <Ranges />
    </AxQuerySimpleEmbeddedDataSource>
</DataSources>
Join Modes:

InnerJoin - Inner join
OuterJoin - Left outer join
ExistsJoin - Exists join (semi-join)
NotExistsJoin - Not exists join (anti-join)

5. Ranges Section
5.1 Basic Range
xml<Ranges>
    <AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
        <Name>RangeName</Name>
        <Field>FieldName</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
</Ranges>
5.2 Range with Label and Default Value
xml<AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
    <Name>CreatedDateTimeRange</Name>
    <Field>CreatedDateTime</Field>
    <Label>@YourLabel:LabelId</Label>
    <Value>01/01/2024..12/31/2024</Value>
</AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
5.3 Locked Range (Non-editable by User)
xml<AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
    <Name>StatusRange</Name>
    <Field>Status</Field>
    <Label>@SYS12345</Label>
    <Status>Locked</Status>
    <Value>Active</Value>
</AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
Range Properties:

<Name> - Unique identifier for the range
<Field> - Field name from the data source
<Label> - Label reference (use @LabelFile:LabelId format)
<Value> - Default value or filter expression
<Status> - Values: Locked, Hidden, or omit for editable
<Enabled> - Values: Yes or No

Range Value Formats:

Single value: "ABC"
Multiple values: "ABC,XYZ"
Range: "A..Z" or "01/01/2024..12/31/2024"
Greater than: ">100"
Less than: "<100"
Not equal: "!ABC"

6. Fields Section (Explicit Field Selection)
xml<Fields>
    <AxQuerySimpleDataSourceField>
        <Name>FieldName1</Name>
        <DataSource>DataSourceName</DataSource>
        <Field>FieldName1</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleDataSourceField>
    <AxQuerySimpleDataSourceField>
        <Name>FieldName2</Name>
        <DataSource>DataSourceName</DataSource>
        <Field>FieldName2</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleDataSourceField>
</Fields>
Note: Use <DynamicFields>Yes</DynamicFields> instead if you want all fields.
7. OrderBy Section
xml<OrderBy>
    <AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
        <Name>QueryOrderByField1</Name>
        <DataSource>DataSourceName</DataSource>
        <Field>FieldName1</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
    <AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
        <Name>QueryOrderByField2</Name>
        <DataSource>DataSourceName</DataSource>
        <Direction>Descending</Direction>
        <Field>FieldName2</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
</OrderBy>
Properties:

<Name> - Unique identifier (QueryOrderByField1, QueryOrderByField2, etc.)
<DataSource> - Data source name
<Field> - Field name to sort by
<Direction> - Values: Ascending (default) or Descending

8. GroupBy Section
xml<GroupBy>
    <AxQuerySimpleGroupByField>
        <Name>GroupByField1</Name>
        <DataSource>DataSourceName</DataSource>
        <Field>FieldName</Field>
    </AxQuerySimpleGroupByField>
</GroupBy>
9. Having Section (Used with GroupBy)
xml<Having>
    <AxQuerySimpleHavingRange>
        <Name>HavingRange1</Name>
        <Field>AggregateField</Field>
        <Value>&gt;100</Value>
    </AxQuerySimpleHavingRange>
</Having>
Note: XML special characters must be escaped:

> as &gt;
< as &lt;
& as &amp;

Complete Example: DocuHistory Cleanup Query
xml<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<AxQuery xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns="" i:type="AxQuerySimple">
    <Name>DocuHistoryCleanupQuery</Name>
    <SourceCode>
        <Methods>
            <Method>
                <Name>classDeclaration</Name>
                <Source><![CDATA[
[Query]
public class DocuHistoryCleanupQuery extends QueryRun
{
}
]]></Source>
            </Method>
        </Methods>
    </SourceCode>
    <DataSources>
        <AxQuerySimpleRootDataSource>
            <Name>DocuHistory</Name>
            <DynamicFields>Yes</DynamicFields>
            <Table>DocuHistory</Table>
            <DataSources />
            <DerivedDataSources />
            <Fields />
            <Ranges>
                <AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
                    <Name>CreatedDateTime</Name>
                    <Field>CreatedDateTime</Field>
                    <Label>@SYS123456</Label>
                </AxQuerySimpleDataSourceRange>
            </Ranges>
            <GroupBy />
            <Having />
            <OrderBy>
                <AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
                    <Name>QueryOrderByField1</Name>
                    <DataSource>DocuHistory</DataSource>
                    <Field>CreatedDateTime</Field>
                </AxQuerySimpleOrderByField>
            </OrderBy>
        </AxQuerySimpleRootDataSource>
    </DataSources>
</AxQuery>
Best Practices
1. Naming Conventions

Query name: Use PascalCase with module prefix
Data source names: Use table names
Range names: Use descriptive field-based names
OrderBy names: Use QueryOrderByField1, QueryOrderByField2, etc.

2. Performance Considerations

Use <DynamicFields>Yes</DynamicFields> unless you need specific field selection
Add appropriate indexes to filtered fields
Use ranges to limit data retrieval
Consider using ExistsJoin instead of InnerJoin for existence checks

3. Labeling

Always provide labels for ranges that users will see
Use existing system labels when applicable
Create custom labels in your label file for specific business terms
Format: @LabelFile:LabelId (e.g., @SYS12345 or @MyModule:MyLabel)

4. Range Configuration

Leave ranges unlocked unless there's a business requirement
Set locked ranges for system-controlled filters
Provide sensible default values when appropriate
Use date range format for DateTime fields: "01/01/2024.."

5. Code Organization

Keep query logic in the query class when possible
Use init() method for dynamic range setup
Override executeQuery() for custom execution logic
Document complex ranges and joins

Common Query Operations in Code
Accessing the Query
csharpQuery query = new Query(queryStr(DocuHistoryCleanupQuery));
QueryRun queryRun = new QueryRun(query);
Modifying Ranges Programmatically
csharpQueryBuildDataSource qbds;
QueryBuildRange qbr;

qbds = query.dataSourceTable(tableNum(DocuHistory));
qbr = qbds.findRange(fieldNum(DocuHistory, CreatedDateTime));

if (!qbr)
{
    qbr = qbds.addRange(fieldNum(DocuHistory, CreatedDateTime));
}

qbr.value(queryValue(cleanupToDate));
Executing the Query
csharpwhile (queryRun.next())
{
    DocuHistory docuHistory = queryRun.get(tableNum(DocuHistory));
    // Process record
}
Troubleshooting
Common Issues

Query not found in AOT

Verify XML filename matches <Name> element
Rebuild the model
Synchronize database


Range not appearing in dialog

Check that range is not set to <Status>Hidden</Status>
Verify label reference is correct
Ensure field exists in the table


Locked range still editable

Verify <Status>Locked</Status> is set
Check for code that might override the range


Performance issues

Verify indexes exist on range fields
Check for missing DynamicFields setting
Review join types and relationships



Related Files
When creating a query, you may also need to update:

Label file (.xml in AxLabelFile folder)
Security privileges (to grant access)
Menu items (to call the query)

Validation Checklist

 XML is well-formed and valid
 Query name matches filename
 All labels are defined
 Data source table exists in AOT
 Range fields exist in table
 Join relationships are correct
 Default values are appropriate
 Performance considerations addressed
 Security access configured
 Query tested with data
